match.reason: None of the bank points teaches rationalising a surd denominator; the closest matches cover adding fractions, complex conjugates (a related but different idea for Victorian Units 1 and 2), equations with fractions and partial fractions, none of which fit this Stage 5 surds point.

draft.title: Rationalising the denominator
card: A fraction with a surd in the denominator, such as \(\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}}\), is not in simplest form. Rationalising means rewriting it so the denominator is a whole number.
Multiply the top and bottom by the surd in the denominator. This is the same as multiplying by 1, so the value does not change.
The denominator becomes a whole number, because \(\sqrt{a} \times \sqrt{a} = a\). The numerator is multiplied by the same surd.
\(\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{6 \times \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}} = \frac{6\sqrt{3}}{3} = 2\sqrt{3}\). Divide the whole numbers at the end if you can.
draft.remember: Multiply top and bottom by the denominator's surd, so the bottom becomes a whole number.

a.q: Which step rationalises the denominator of \(\frac{10}{\sqrt{5}}\)?
opts: Multiply the top and bottom by \(\sqrt{5}\)
Multiply the top and bottom by 5
Divide the top and bottom by \(\sqrt{5}\)
a.why: Multiplying the top and bottom by \(\sqrt{5}\) keeps the value the same and makes the bottom \(\sqrt{5} \times \sqrt{5} = 5\). Multiplying only the top changes the value of the fraction.
a.clue: Multiply by a fraction equal to 1, using the surd on the bottom.

b.q: Rationalise the denominator of \(\frac{12}{\sqrt{6}}\) and simplify.
b.why: \(\frac{12}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{12\sqrt{6}}{6} = 2\sqrt{6}\). Leaving it as \(12\sqrt{6}\) forgets to divide by the new denominator 6.
b.clue: After multiplying, the denominator is 6. Divide 12 by it.

a.best: Multiply the top and bottom by \(\sqrt{5}\)
